thread:
IncidentBot: P1 pager -> streaming /v1/generate in us-west-2. Error rate jumped to ~5% over the last 5m, p95 latency from 250ms -> 1.4s. Affected: hosted customers on prod. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-20260310-7 :rotating_light:

Sam K: I’m primary for the next 2h, taking this. Quick triage notes below. Priya you’re secondary, can you confirm GPU pool and KV cache metrics? Matt you’re on fallback routing if we need to switch models.

Priya R: Looking now - GPU pool utilization at 65% overall but one shard (dedicated-pool-3) shows 92% mem and 88% compute. KV cache evictions spiked ~08:31 UTC. Pulling logs for that shard.

Sam K: OK possible hotspot + cache thrash. Initial mitigation plan: 1) scale ded-pool-3 by +1 replica (if autoscale not keeping up) 2) enable prefix-KV read-only fallback for hot prefixes 3) temp route low-priority traffic to smaller model rwd-7b-quant to reduce pressure. If errors persist, open a rollback to stable routing.

Oncall Bot: Handoff/runbook quick links:
- Runbook: Streaming API spike remediation -> https://runbooks.internal/redwood/streaming-spike
- Scale GPU pool -> https://runbooks.internal/redwood/scale-dedicated-pool
- KV cache tuning -> https://runbooks.internal/redwood/kv-cache-troubleshoot
- Routing fallback -> https://runbooks.internal/redwood/routing-fallback

Priya R: Scaling now. Command I ran:```bash
infra-cli scale pool dedicated-pool-3 --replicas 3 --region us-west-2
``` logs show scale accepted, new node provisioning. ETA ~90s for node ready.

Sam K: While the node comes up, can someone run quick tail on worker errors? Use this:```bash
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=worker -c runtime --since=5m | grep -i "rpc error\|timeout\|oom" | tail -n 200
``` Looking for stacktrace that indicates KV or OOM.

Tanya V: I ran that and see repeated `KVGetTimeout` and a few `OOM on allocation` traces on ded-pool-3 workers. Also a handful of 429s from the rate-limiter service consistent with burst exceeding token bucket.

Sam K: Good signal. Immediate mitigations applied: 1) Increased rate-limiter burst in us-west-2 config (temporary) 2) Enabled read-only KV fallback for top-10 prefixes (to avoid heavy writes) 3) Route 15% of traffic to rwd-7b-quant via rollout policy `rollout/low-latency-fallback`.

Priya R: New node joined, pod distribution rebalanced. ded-pool-3 memory pressure dropping. Error count down from 5% -> ~1.2% in last 3m.

Matt L: Confirmed routing change propagated to API gateway. I also kicked off a canary request set from our synthetic runner to validate correctness. All canary responses look within SLO and no increased hallucination observed.

Sam K: Customer impact assessment: small subset of low-priority hosts saw degraded throughput for ~10m window. No data exfiltration risk. SLO breach likely for 1 customer tier; will file post-incident note.

Oncall Bot: Quick remediation checklist (paste into next-handoff):
- Primary/secondary set: Sam K (primary) -> Priya R (secondary)
- Key runbooks used: streaming-spike, scale-dedicated-pool, kv-cache-troubleshoot, routing-fallback
- Actions taken: scaled dedicated-pool-3, increased rate-limiter burst, KV read-only fallback, routed 15% traffic to smaller model
- Current status: degrading -> recovering, error rate ~1.2%, p95 ~420ms
- Next steps: monitor 30m, rollback routing if error rate not <1% after 15m, prepare customer comms if SLO confirmed breached.

Priya R: I'll be primary after Sam's block ends (in ~25m). Leaving these notes in the incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/INC-20260310-7/notes

Sam K: Thanks team - writing a concise handoff for the next shift:
1) What to watch: ded-pool-3 mem/cpu, KV eviction rate, rate-limiter 429s, p95 latency for /v1/generate
2) Quick fixes:
   - If OOMs persist: cordon pool node -> drain -> reprovision (runbook link above)
   - If KV timeouts: enable higher read-timeout + prefix-only writes (see KV runbook)
   - If p95 stays high but errors low: scale serving replicas or route more to quantized variant
3) Escalation path: if error rate >3% for 10m, page SRE escalation channel and exec on-call.

Matt L: Noted. I'll keep synthetic checks running and tag you both on any regression. :white_check_mark:

Sam K: leaving final ephemeral note: handing primary to Priya in 18m, I’ll remain reachable if anything flares. — Sam

Priya R: Got it - taking over at T+18m. Will consolidate logs and update incident doc. :wave:
